h1: How to automate lead follow-up from Gmail
answer: Keep a lead list with a stage and a last-contact date, and each morning draft a follow-up in the same thread for leads quiet three days.
Stop the moment anyone from their side replies.

sections.h2: What Gmail can do on its own

body.p: Gmail can remind you, not send for you: its nudges suggest emails to follow up on. To draft or send follow-ups, you need an add-on (GMass, Mixmax and others), a CRM with sequences, or an automation tool that reads your Gmail.

Whatever you use sends from your account, so Gmail's limits apply: up to 2,000 messages a day for a Workspace user, around 500 for personal Gmail. Hitting the limit stops all your sending for up to 24 hours.

method.h2: How to automate lead follow-up from Gmail, step by step

steps.title: Make the lead list
steps.body: Name, email, company, stage (New, Contacted, Replied, Won, Lost), last contact and next follow-up. A sheet or a CRM both work; the columns are what matter.

steps.title: Set the gap and the count
steps.body: Three days for warm leads, a week for cold ones, and two or three follow-ups at most. Write it down; it becomes the rule.

steps.title: Write each follow-up to move one step
steps.body: Not "just checking in". Offer the next step: a call time, a shorter version of the quote, a question that is easy to answer.

steps.title: Send in the same thread
steps.body: A reply in the original thread keeps the context for the lead and keeps reply detection simple.

steps.title: Check for replies before every send
steps.body: Read the thread just before sending, not only when the list was last updated. Count a reply from anyone at their domain as a reply.

note.text: An out-of-office is not a reply. Treat "automatic reply" messages as quiet, and follow up after their return date.

steps.title: Update the list after each email
steps.body: Last contact to today, next follow-up to the next gap, and a note of what you sent.

captain.line: Captain builds a leads app with a pipeline board and an AI agent that drafts each follow-up in the original thread once a lead goes quiet. You approve every one.

wrong.title: A follow-up after they replied
wrong.body: They answered from a colleague's address, or started a new thread. Check the thread and their domain right before each send.

wrong.title: Your whole Gmail stops sending
wrong.body: A big sequence hit the daily limit, which blocks all your mail, not just the automation. Keep automated sends well under it.

wrong.title: Follow-ups at 3 in the morning
wrong.body: The tool ran in another timezone. Set sends for working hours in the lead's timezone where you know it.

wrong.title: The same email three times
wrong.body: Each follow-up is a copy of the first. Write each one to offer something new, or stop after one.

faqs.q: Does Gmail have automatic follow-ups built in?
faqs.a: No. Gmail's nudges remind you to follow up; they do not send anything. Sending needs an add-on, a CRM sequence or an automation tool.

faqs.q: How long should I wait before following up with a lead?
faqs.a: Two to three working days for a lead who asked you something, a week for a cold contact. Stop after two or three follow-ups with no reply.

faqs.q: Will automated follow-ups hurt my deliverability?
faqs.a: A few dozen personal follow-ups in the same thread will not. Hundreds of near-identical emails a day from one account can, and they also risk Gmail's sending limits.
